title: Monthly temperature gave no repeated gain in later-year cherry bloom interval estimates in Japan in 1981-2025
abstract: We tested whether fixed monthly temperature improved estimates of the time from first to full cherry bloom in later years. We used 3,100 paired records at 48 Japanese stations in 1961-2025. Models were trained only on earlier years. Four tests used two regions and two later periods. Temperature changed mean absolute error by gains of -0.089, +0.090, +0.156 and +0.053 days. Only northern Japan in 2003-2025 had a primary adjusted interval above zero. Its gain fell to +0.004 days without a time trend. Thus this simple model gave no repeated gain across regions and periods. Monthly weather can extend past bloom, so this is not an operational forecast. Selected stations, missing tree and visit records, coarse weather and uncertainty conditional on training fits limit the result. We do not test pollution, daily extremes or a causal climate effect.

display.caption: Mean absolute error gain from monthly temperature in four later-year tests. Positive values mean lower error. Bars are 98.75 percent circular time-block intervals conditional on training fits.
